page: Amazon Web Services g7e.48xlarge is a high-density accelerated computing instance designed for distributed machine learning, graphics rendering, and heavy computational pipelines. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 2.4 GHz, backed by 320 MB of L3 cache and hardware acceleration flags including AVX-512 and AMX. The host integrates 2,048 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, alongside an accelerator array of eight NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs providing 768 GB of aggregate VRAM. Local high-speed storage is bundled via 15,200 GB of NVMe SSDs, supported by a 1,600 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations confirm exceptional throughput across multiple parallel dimensions. The platform achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (169,929.73) and PassMark CPU metrics (131,267.39), with extended vector instructions scoring 210,731.32. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 447.23 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 1,101.51 GB/sec. In large language model evaluation, the architecture achieves 1,269.37 prompt processing tokens per second and 28.08 generation tokens per second on 70B parameter models, while handling 7,046.47 prompt processing tokens per second on 7B models. In-memory data throughput is equally robust, registering 201.69 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance consolidates substantial compute, expansive high-speed DDR5 memory, massive local NVMe capacity, and extreme networking into a single bare-metal-equivalent footprint. This density reduces the overhead of inter-node communication across distributed clusters. A primary tradeoff involves resource utilization: workloads unable to saturate 192 vCPUs, eight high-end GPUs, and extreme network bandwidth simultaneously may encounter resource underutilization relative to smaller specialized instances.

The AWS g7e.48xlarge is best suited for large language model fine-tuning and inference, distributed 3D rendering, large-scale ray tracing, parallel scientific simulations, and high-throughput in-memory database processing.
description: Amazon Web Services g7e.48xlarge is a flagship accelerated computing instance built on the Nitro hypervisor for intensive graphics, AI, and distributed compute workloads. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 2.4 GHz with AVX-512 and AMX support, paired with 2,048 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory. The instance bundles eight NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs delivering 768 GB of total VRAM, supplemented by 15,200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 1,600 Gbps of baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations reflect top-tier results in multi-core CPU execution, vector processing, Redis operations, and LLM prompt processing. Delivering high compute and memory density within a single node, it minimizes distributed communication overhead, making it well matched for generative AI inference, multi-GPU rendering, ray tracing, and memory-intensive database engines.
